abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Malnutrition because of the deficiency of minerals such as iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn) afflicts over 2 billion people worldwide. Wheat is a major staple crop, providing 20% of dietary energy and protein consumption worldwide. Breeding wheat with elevated levels of grain Zn and Fe concentrations (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GZn</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GFe</jats:styled-content>) represents a significant opportunity to increase the intake of these micronutrients for the resource poor people who depend on it as a major source of dietary energy. Synthetic hexaploid wheats (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SHWs</jats:styled-content>) have large genetic variation for <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GZn</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GFe</jats:styled-content>, which can be exploited for developing wheat varieties with higher concentrations of these minerals. The objective of this study was to localise genomic regions associated with <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GZn</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GFe</jats:styled-content>, thousand kernel weight (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TKW</jats:styled-content>) and test weight (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TW</jats:styled-content>) in a mapping population derived from the cross of Seri <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">M82</jats:styled-content> and the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SHW CWI76364</jats:styled-content>. Major quantitative trait loci (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content>) on chromosome <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">4BS</jats:styled-content> were detected for <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GZn</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GFe</jats:styled-content>; the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> explained up to 19.6% of the total phenotypic variation for <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GZn</jats:styled-content> and showed pleiotropic effects on <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GFe</jats:styled-content>. This indicates that simultaneous improvement of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GZn</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GFe</jats:styled-content> is feasible. Three and five <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> for <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TW</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TKW</jats:styled-content> were detected, respectively. One of the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> for <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TKW</jats:styled-content> was also located on chromosome <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">4BS</jats:styled-content>. Positive correlations between plant height and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GZn</jats:styled-content>/<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GFe</jats:styled-content> were observed. The <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">4BS QTL</jats:styled-content> is of great interest for breeding biofortified wheat by means of marker‐assisted selection.</jats:p>
title: Quantitative trait loci mapping reveals pleiotropic effect for grain iron and zinc concentrations in wheat
